item.text: {"text":"Evidence favors testing adaptive hardness, not assuming it beats uniform sampling. A [2024 sequential-recommendation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) compared random, popularity, in-batch, mixed and adaptive sampling across three datasets with hyperparameter optimization and 20 repeats. Random sampling favored head items; popularity-based alternatives improved balance but could reduce aggregate accuracy. [Curricular weighting research (2024)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S002002552400447X) supports easy-to-hard negative weighting and regularization against false negatives, although its evidence concerns contrastive learning rather than BERT4Rec masked-item candidate cross entropy. Earlier [RealHNS](https://ercdm.sdu.edu.cn/__local/3/11/1F/4813FCDEA9F8F773BE1ECBDDBA6_121A6BF4_196B08.pdf) combines curriculum learning with false-hard-negative filtering in cross-domain recommendation; transfer to this setting remains unverified.\n\nPractical hypothesis: retain one BERT4Rec per category and K=16 negatives; warm up uniformly, then gradually emphasize moderately high-scoring negatives using the same network. Exclude known training positives and duplicate candidates; retain random coverage. Highest score alone cannot establish that an item is a true negative. Compare uniform K=16 against curriculum weighting of the same 16 candidates first, avoiding extra mining-pool scoring; measure GPU time, positive–negative margins and negative softmax concentration. Treat this as an experiment, since the sources located do not establish a matched-K, matched-compute BERT4Rec win. Distinguish candidate cross entropy from an unbiased full-catalog softmax approximation: [NeurIPS 2025 theory](https://papers.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/42b7c2f6d320d1fe1afa899a6319d6d7-Abstract-Conference.html) establishes limitations of unbiased sampled softmax estimators. Select using the fixed macro validation HR@10; current diagnostics provide no measured margin evidence justifying aggressive mining."}
